script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for July 5. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Where are your keys?  Your important documents?  That thing you need right now?

The secret of organized people: everything has a designated place. Keys go on the hook. Papers go in the file. When you finish using something, it returns home. Disorganization happens when things don't have homes—or don't go back. Research shows cluttered environments increase stress hormones.  Visual noise competes for attention.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: External order supports internal order.  Organization teaches that environment shapes mind.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is One Home - Reduce Finding Friction.

Here's your activity: Choose one thing you frequently lose or search for. Give it a home—a specific place it always goes. Practice returning it there until it becomes automatic. One good system beats a hundred good intentions. This helps you create systems for commonly lost items.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about putting things in order can be applied to one home - reduce finding friction. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
